transcript:
Meeting header
Date/Time: 2027-03-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), David Ortiz (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood Partner Ops), Samir Khalid (Emberlane Head of GTM), Ruth Delgado (Emberlane Channel Sales), Tom Briggs (Emberlane VP Partnerships), Aisha Noor (Emberlane Solutions Architect)

Auto-summary: alignment on co-sell plays, prioritize accounts, send security artifacts, run perf check for Acme Health POC

--- Transcript (timestamps approximate, auto-transcript, some words garbled) ---
00:00 Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, uh let's do quick intros, we have about 50 minutes so we'll be tight
00:07 Samir Khalid: yeah appreciate it, hey all Samir here, we'll keep it high level — we have a gaggle of deals to triage so excited to sync
00:13 David Ortiz: David, infra / se side, I'll own the perf checks and quick technical triage items
00:18 Ruth Delgado: Ruth from channel, I manage partner reps and handoffs
00:21 Hannah Li: Hannah, partner ops redwood, I'll handle paperwork and co-sell assets
00:26 Tom Briggs: Tom — pipelining and executive introductions from Emberlane side
00:29 Aisha Noor: Aisha, solutions, I'll help map technical requirements
00:33 Maya Chen: Cool. Agenda — quick status of top six joint accounts, pick top 2 for immediate co-sell, discuss pilots + success criteria, security ask, and next steps. Any additions?
00:45 Samir Khalid: nope that's perfect. First account: Acme Health — they've asked for a POC by two weeks and care a lot about data residency and audit logs
00:56 Maya Chen: right, we recommended Redwood Dedicated for regulated workloads but there's options — private deployment as a conversation if they need full on-prem. question for you Aisha, do they require on-prem or is VPC enough?
01:08 Aisha Noor: initial ask is VPC + bring-your-own-key via KMS, they said SOC2 plus iso-27001 would be needed, maybe on-prem later but start with VPC.
01:20 David Ortiz: that maps well. For VPC we can do the private control plane and KMS. Latency wise, with our Dedicated SKUs we can hit their SLOs; but we should vet token volumes, sequence length distribution. If they stream long transcripts it's a different story.
01:34 Ruth Delgado: commercial ask — what's the expected ARR from Acme? We need to understand commercial model for revenue split.
01:40 Samir Khalid: estimated ARR 350k annually if pilot converts, champion is Dr. Patel. Timeline is tight — exec intro this week would help.
01:48 Maya Chen: ACTION: schedule exec intro. Ruth can you take point?
01:52 Ruth Delgado: yes, I'll organize that.
01:54 Tom Briggs: second deal — GlobalFab manufacturing — bigger, cross-border controls, data residency in EU and APAC, they might demand air-gapped for some lines.
02:06 David Ortiz: air-gapped is in scope for private on-prem but that becomes a bespoke engagement. We should label that high risk.
02:12 Maya Chen: Agreed, mark as high risk. We need to get legal and eng on that early. Samir, is GlobalFab one of your target top 8?
02:18 Samir Khalid: yes, high priority.
02:21 Maya Chen: Good. Quick poll — of the six deals which two do we push to immediate co-sell? I propose Acme Health and NovaBank (regulated financial). Thoughts?
02:34 Ruth Delgado: NovaBank is sticky, they want on-prem eventually but pilot is just sandbox. we can pilot in VPC.
02:41 Aisha Noor: NovaBank also cares about redaction workflows and PII handling, we'll need to map that to Redwood's audit logs and redaction tooling, sometimes transcript has misreads so they want deterministic redaction.
02:53 David Ortiz: We have prefix/KV cache and batching knobs; cost/latency trade will matter to them. If we push batching for cost we'll increase tail latency, so for bank I'd recommend lower batch sizes and reserved capacity during pilot.
03:05 Maya Chen: Great technical nuance. Pricing — Emberlane expects a margin on co-sell. Typical structure: 70/30 net-retain? we can be flexible. Hannah, what's acceptable?
03:16 Hannah Li: we need to stay within our channel guidelines, usually mid 20s percent commission for reseller, but for strategic deals we can negotiate carveouts. we'll model both a rev-share and a referral fee.
03:26 Tom Briggs: Emberlane needs an example contract addendum to show procurement — can Redwood share sample SOW language?
03:33 Maya Chen: yes, we'll share a short SOW template and partner addendum. ACTION: Maya to drop docs.
03:39 Samir Khalid: Security checklist — we need SOC2 report, encryption in transit at rest, KMS detail, and audit log retention policies. Also, can Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
03:50 Hannah Li: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for private and VPC with our integrations — I'll attach KMS notes. SOC2 is fine, we'll share report, but note some items redacted for vendor info.
04:02 Aisha Noor: how about logging? we need per-request audit logs and token-level tracing for the regulator.
04:09 David Ortiz: we produce per-request traces and console-level token breakdowns in Redwood Console; for private, we can forward logs to customer's SIEM via secure channel. caveat: retention varies by plan.
04:25 Ruth Delgado: question from my reps — if we run a POC and they need lower latency than hosted, do we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private?
04:34 David Ortiz: Dedicated is best balance: predictable throughput and lower tail latency with reserved capacity. Private on-prem for extreme compliance. But Dedicated can be deployed in customer region to satisfy residency.
04:47 Samir Khalid: any benchmarking we can show vs OpenAI? Customers always ask this.
04:52 David Ortiz: we can do a short perf vs competitor run for the POC — smaller prompt sets, measure latency and cost per 1k tokens. it'll be a sanity check more than a full bench. ACTION: David to run perf sanity.
05:03 Maya Chen: Good. Commercial questions — contract length, support SLAs, excess usage. Hannah?
05:10 Hannah Li: Dedicated comes with SLA and we can offer enterprise support with 24/7 pager on certain tiers. We'll include a pricing stub in the packet.
05:18 Tom Briggs: Risk: a few accounts need regulatory approvals before pipeline can progress — let's tag those and involve compliance early.
05:26 Maya Chen: We'll tag GlobalFab and NovaBank as compliance-heavy. Also, Acme needs audit logs and KMS only.
05:33 Samir Khalid: For Acme, can Redwood do PII redaction in model responses or do we need pre-/post-processing?
05:40 David Ortiz: we recommend pre-processing for structured PII redaction and post-checks for generated content. We also support function-calling style outputs to make structures stricter. Note: transcription sometimes mislabels proper nouns so we should test with their data.
05:58 Ruth Delgado: Sales enablement — Emberlane wants co-branded one-pager and a champion email template for outreach.
06:04 Maya Chen: We'll provide a co-branded one-pager and templated email. ACTION: Maya.
06:10 Samir Khalid: timeline — Acme pilot kickoff target next Tue, can we get exec intro before then?
06:16 Ruth Delgado: I'll coordinate and send invites today.
06:19 Maya Chen: Nice. Recap of open risks: GlobalFab on-prem requirement (high risk), NovaBank regulatory redaction needs (medium-high), Acme timeline + residency (medium).
06:30 Tom Briggs: Any competitive intel? some buyers are vetting OpenAI and Anthropic; Emberlane differentiator is reseller relationship and go-to-market coverage.
06:40 Hannah Li: we'll prepare a short competitive positioning doc for partner reps.
06:45 Samir Khalid: One minor thing — we may need a special pricing carve for public sector in EU, can discuss later.
06:50 Maya Chen: ok last thing — handoff checklist: we need champion contact, tech contacts, legal procurement timeline, expected ARR, and success metric for pilot. Can Emberlane fill those in the account list?
07:02 Samir Khalid: yes will do.
07:06 Maya Chen: Great. Let's summarize next steps and owners.
07:10 Ruth Delgado: quick Q: does Redwood support canary rollouts across model variants?
07:14 David Ortiz: yes, Redwood Console supports rollouts/canary and automatic fallback to smaller models if a variant errors out. The routing policies can use region and cost thresholds.
07:26 Maya Chen: perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with packet and calendar invites.
07:32 Meeting end

--- End transcript ---
